## Purpose

These rules keep the laboratory safe, clean and working for everyone. They apply to all users of the EnGeL laboratory: staff, students, visitors and collaborators. Each protocol adds the safety points specific to its method.

## Lab rules

{{< include ../includes/_safety-general.qmd >}}

- **Safety equipment:** know where the first-aid kits and fire extinguishers are, and where the containers for hazardous waste, sharps and glass are.
- **Reagents:** store all reagents and products properly and clearly labelled. Do not store materials or reagents at the workstations.
- **Common-use equipment:** never touch computers, balances, phones or other shared equipment with contaminated gloves.
- **Questions:** ask your supervisor before using a chemical or a piece of equipment you are not sure about.

## Cleaning, stocks and shared materials

- **Work areas:** keep equipment and benches clean and organised. Replace waste bags when full.
- **Restocking:** every user restocks distilled water, paper towels, TBE/TAE buffer and ethanol in the work areas, and tells the stock manager when supplies run low.
- **Consumables:** general consumables (ethanol, detergents, autoclave tape and similar) are managed by a designated person [TO CONFIRM: who]. Report low stocks of kits and PCR consumables to your supervisor.
- **Non-disposable materials:** rinse with tap water and leave them in the washing tubs near the EnGeL sink. When the designated person is away, users wash their own materials.
- **Annual cleaning:** two cleaning days a year, on the last Friday of March and of September. Everyone takes part.

## Waste

{{< include ../includes/_waste-streams.qmd >}}

The 2024 lab procedure also mentions contaminated waste that is autoclaved before disposal [TO CONFIRM: does this still apply, and for which waste?]. Autoclaving is described in the [autoclave procedure](equipment/EnGeL-GUIDE-AUTOCLAVE.qmd).

## Equipment

- Switch equipment on and off as its procedure requires; always switch off the heating of shakers and stirrers after use.
- Book shared equipment (thermocyclers, centrifuges, autoclave and others) on the weekly registration sheets, and record use in the equipment logs ([Equipment](equipment/index.qmd)).
- Report any fault to the responsible researcher.

## Samples, ice and liquid nitrogen

- Tell the designated person when samples arrive [TO CONFIRM: who], and label and store them as described in [Sample labelling and storage](EnGeL-GUIDE-SAMPLES.qmd).
- Use ice sparingly. For liquid nitrogen, talk to Luís Cunha [TO CONFIRM: how deliveries are organised].

## Freezers, fridges and power cuts

- Clean and defrost freezers and fridges regularly; keep everything labelled and discard what is no longer needed.
- Report power cuts immediately and do not open freezers or fridges during a cut.

## Incidents

Report incidents, accidents and equipment faults to your scientific supervisor, or by e-mail to the lab contact.

## Before you leave

{{< include ../includes/_before-you-leave.qmd >}}

At the end of the day, or when you are the last person in the lab, check that equipment and lights are off and that doors and windows are closed.
